overall: The AG found the Falmouth School Committee violated the Law by posting a September 10 notice that omitted the bargaining unit and grievance nature for a Purpose 3 executive session, but found no violation in approving July 16 minutes on time.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the September 10 notice failed to identify the collective bargaining unit discussed in executive session under Purpose 3.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee has not demonstrated that identifying the bargaining unit and the nature of the discussion reasonably may have compromised its bargaining position with regard to the grievance discussed at the September 10 meeting, the Committee’s failure to include that information on the meeting notice violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee did not timely approve its July 16 minutes, approving them at its September 10 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Law when it approved the July 16 meeting minutes during its September 10 meeting, as that was the third meeting the Committee held following its July 16 meeting.

allegations.summary: Not raised in complaint: the AG noted executive session discussion of private schools and other bargaining units, neither listed on the notice, and questioned whether they were proper.
allegations.key_passage: Neither topic was included on the notice for the September 10 meeting, nor is it clear that either topic was appropriate for executive session.

allegations.summary: Not raised in complaint: the AG noted procedural lapses entering executive session, such as no stated purpose and no Purpose 3 statement, and roll call votes not recorded.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, although not raised in the complaint, we note several concerns with the manner in which the Committee conducted its executive session, and we recommend that the Committee review our training video on executive sessions and our checklist for entering into executive session.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law and may result in imposition of a penalty.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
